sourcedFrom:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 (2021)
cleanIntro: The SRD22X is fully user-serviceable and rimfire fouling makes that necessary — seven baffles come out of a titanium tube and get cleaned individually. Two things bound this procedure: the host firearm has its own manual that governs alongside this one, and the rear cap is bonded in and never comes out.

steps.title: This manual is only half of what governs your setup
steps.action: Before anything else, read this suppressor's manual AND the operator's manual for the host firearm it is mounted on. The host's book covers clearing that firearm, its thread pitch and its own restrictions — none of which are in this document.
steps.prose: This is not a formality. A suppressor manual cannot tell you how to unload the gun it is screwed to, and the SRD22X mounts on a range of .22 pistols and rifles that clear in completely different ways. Get the host cleared using the host's own procedure before you touch the suppressor.
steps.quote: WARNING: READ THIS MANUAL AND THE OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR THE HOST FIREARM IN THEIR ENTIRETY BEFORE OPERATING THIS SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — Cover warning, p.1
steps.warn: Never install or remove this suppressor from a firearm that has not been both visually and physically cleared of all ammunition.

steps.title: Host chambering — the enumerated list, not 'any rimfire'
steps.action: Confirm your host is one SIG covers. The SRD22X is a direct-thread suppressor for .22 caliber pistols and rifles, and SIG states that because of its materials it can be used with .22 LR pistols and rifles chambered in .17 HMR, .17 Mach II and .22 Magnum. That is the list. A cartridge outside it is not covered by this document.
steps.prose: Host limits are model-specific to each suppressor and do not carry across from one SIG can to another — what the SRD22X's Grade 9 titanium tube and seven stainless baffles will take is not what a different suppressor's construction will take. Do not reason from another suppressor's ratings to this one.
steps.quote: Due to the durability of its materials, the SRD22X can be used with .22LR pistols and rifles chambered in .17HMR/.17 Mach II and .22 Magnum.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 2.1 Specifications, p.10

steps.title: Ammunition types SIG forbids through this suppressor
steps.action: Check what you have been shooting and what is on the bench. Pre-fragmented (frangible), multi-projectile, segmented, tracer and shot cartridges must not be fired through SIG rimfire suppressors.
steps.prose: Firing any of them through the SRD22X can produce a fragment hazard to the shooter and damage the suppressor or the host firearm. If you suspect any of these has gone through it, treat the can as suspect and inspect the baffles carefully during the strip below rather than assuming it is fine because it still sounds right.
steps.quote: Do not fire pre-fragmented (frangible), multi-projectile, segmented, tracer or shot cartridges through SIG SAUER Rimfire suppressors.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 1.2 Ammunition, p.6

steps.title: Let it cool, and check what it has been through
steps.action: Do not start work on a hot suppressor. If accuracy fell off suddenly during the session, or you saw a tumbled impact on target, stop and treat the disassembly below as an inspection: check the suppressor is still tight to the barrel and look over the end cap for strike marks.
steps.prose: Suppressors get hot enough in normal use to burn skin and to ignite what they are set down on, so wear heat-resistant gloves and do not put a just-fired can on anything that can be damaged. Discolouration of the tube is the visible sign it has been run too hard.
steps.quote: If you suspect the suppressor has suffered a baffle or end cap strike immediately stop shooting, clear and unload the firearm:
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 1.3 Baffle Strike, p.7
steps.warn: A known baffle strike is a stop-work condition, not a maintenance item. Contact customer service for repair rather than shooting it again.

steps.title: Off the host, by hand
steps.action: With the host firearm cleared, unthread the suppressor from the muzzle by hand. Do not put the suppressor wrench on it to remove it from the firearm.
steps.prose: The SRD22X threads on hand-tight by design — SIG's installation instruction is to screw it on as tight as you can by hand and to keep the wrench off the job. The wrench exists for the end cap, not for the mount, and using it on the mount is how threads get galled on an aluminium-receivered .22.
steps.quote: Align the threaded muzzle of the barrel with the suppressor and screw the suppressor on as tight as you can by hand.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 3.2 Attaching SRD22X Suppressor - Continued, step 4, p.14

steps.title: Front end cap off with the wrench — and no vise
steps.action: Use the SRD22 wrench to unscrew and remove the front end cap. Hold the suppressor in your hands or in a soft-jawed holder that does not squeeze the tube.
steps.prose: SIG is explicit that the tube must not be clamped in a vise: the Grade 9 titanium tube will deform, and a deformed tube traps the baffles so they cannot be driven out at all. Rimfire fouling can seize the cap after a long session, so soak the joint rather than reaching for more leverage.
steps.caution: Do not clamp the suppressor tube in a vise — SIG warns it can damage the tube and prevent removal of the baffles.
steps.quote: Use the SRD22 wrench to unscrew and remove the front end cap.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.1 Disassemble the SRD22X, step 1, p.15

steps.title: Rear cap stays — it is bonded in
steps.action: Do not attempt to remove the rear cap. It is bonded to the suppressor tube and is not a serviceable joint.
steps.prose: There is nothing to gain by trying: the baffles come out of the front, so the rear cap does not need to move for a full clean. Working at it damages the bond and the tube, and neither is repairable at owner level.
steps.quote: The rear cap is bonded to the suppressor tube and should not be removed.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.1 Disassemble the SRD22X - Continued, note, p.16

steps.title: All seven baffles out of the tube
steps.action: Tip the baffles out of the front of the tube and count them — there are seven. Note which way round they sit as they come out; the rounded edge faces forward.
steps.prose: Count them out and count them back in. Rimfire fouling can weld baffles to each other and to the tube, and a stack that comes out as one lump is easy to miscount. Look at each one as you separate it for the bright scoring or clipped edge that a strike leaves.
steps.quote: Remove all seven baffles from the suppressor tube.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.1 Disassemble the SRD22X - Continued, step 2, p.16

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Tube with its bonded rear cap, front end cap, seven baffles, and the M9-.75 adapter if it was fitted. That is the full user-serviceable strip of an SRD22X.
steps.prose: SIG's cleaning interval for this suppressor is every 500 rounds, which is far shorter than a centrefire can because unjacketed .22 bullets deposit lead and wax rather than just carbon. Nothing else on this suppressor comes apart, and adding any component that would lengthen it beyond its original length is unlawful under NFA rules.
steps.quote: The recommended cleaning interval for the SRD22X is every 500 rounds.
steps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.2 Cleaning, p.17

deepSteps.title: Soak the baffles and end cap
deepSteps.action: Put the seven baffles and the front end cap into a firearms solvent and let them soak until the build-up on the internal and external surfaces has loosened.
deepSteps.prose: Soaking is what does the work on rimfire fouling — the lead and wax deposit is soft but tenacious and it does not scrub off dry. An ultrasonic cleaner is approved for this suppressor if you have one; follow its instructions and use a solution compatible with stainless steel and titanium.
deepSteps.caution: Read and follow the solvent manufacturer's warnings, and work in a ventilated space.
deepSteps.quote: Soak baffles and front end cap in solvent to loosen residue build up from internal and external surfaces.
deepSteps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.3 Cleaning-Continued, p.18

deepSteps.title: Scotch-Brite the heavy build-up off the baffles
deepSteps.action: Work the remaining heavy deposit off each baffle with a Scotch-Brite cleaning pad, then wipe the solvent off and dry the baffle.
deepSteps.prose: SIG's approved list for this suppressor is a firearms solvent, a nylon bristle brush and Scotch-Brite pads. Sandpaper, emery cloth and similar abrasives are specifically excluded — they remove material as well as fouling, and on a baffle the internal geometry is what does the suppressing.
deepSteps.quote: Use Scotch-Brite pad to remove heavy build up from baffles.
deepSteps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.3 Cleaning-Continued, p.18
deepSteps.warn: Do not use sandpaper, emery cloth or similar abrasives on any component of this suppressor.

deepSteps.title: End cap body and threads
deepSteps.action: Clean the residue off the front end cap, then clean its threads specifically — the thread form is where the fouling that seizes the cap collects.
deepSteps.prose: A cap that fought you on the way off will fight you again unless the threads are cleaned rather than just the faces. A nylon brush along the thread is enough; do not chase the thread with anything harder.
deepSteps.quote: Clean threads of front end cap.
deepSteps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.3 Cleaning-Continued, p.18

deepSteps.title: Everything dry and oil-free before it goes back together
deepSteps.action: Make sure every component is clean, dry and free of any oil or cleaning solvent before you reassemble the suppressor.
deepSteps.prose: This is not the same rule as a firearm's — a suppressor gets no protective oil film. Solvent or oil left inside the tube burns off on the first shots as smoke and vapour out of the muzzle, and it holds fouling to the baffle faces you just cleaned.
deepSteps.quote: Ensure all components are clean, dry and free from oil or cleaning solvents prior to reassembly.
deepSteps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 4.3 Cleaning-Continued, p.18

deepSteps.title: Baffles back in, rounded edge forward
deepSteps.action: Install the seven baffles into the tube with the rounded edge of each facing forward, toward the muzzle end.
deepSteps.prose: Orientation is the whole job here. A baffle stack installed backwards presents the wrong face to the bullet path and turns the alignment margin into a strike risk. Count all seven in.
deepSteps.quote: Install the seven baffles into the suppressor tube with the rounded edge facing forward.
deepSteps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 5.0 Reassembly, step 1, p.19

deepSteps.title: Front end cap on, hand tight with the wrench
deepSteps.action: Thread the front end cap into the tube by hand, then tighten it by hand using the suppressor wrench.
deepSteps.prose: Hand tight using the wrench — the wrench is there for grip on a knurled cap, not for torque. Over-tightening a titanium tube's threads is a repair job, and the cap does not need more than this to stay put.
deepSteps.quote: Tighten the front end cap by hand using the suppressor wrench.
deepSteps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 5.0 Reassembly, step 3, p.19

deepSteps.title: M9-.75 adapter, only if your host needs it
deepSteps.action: The suppressor ships with a 1/2 x 28 TPI end cap installed and an additional M9-.75 adapter. Fit the adapter only if your host barrel is M9-.75 threaded: clean the end cap and adapter threads, thread the adapter into the end cap, and snug it with an adjustable wrench on the adapter flats.
deepSteps.prose: Identify and match the threads on your muzzle before mounting anything — this suppressor's native interface is 1/2 x 28 right hand. Cross-threading a .22 barrel's muzzle threads is easy and expensive, and it is why SIG's mounting instruction is by hand.
deepSteps.quote: Thread adapter into end cap of suppressor.
deepSteps.cite:
SIG SAUER RIMFIRE SUPPRESSORS
OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 8501926-01 REV 02 — 6.0 Appendix A: Install M9-.75 Adapter, step 2, p.20

cleaning.name: APPROVED MATERIALS ONLY
tasks: Solvent designed for use on firearms
An ultrasonic cleaner is approved — use a solution compatible with stainless steel and titanium
No sandpaper, emery cloth or similar abrasive on any component

cleaning.name: BAFFLES (SEVEN)
tasks: Soak in solvent until the internal and external build-up loosens
Wipe the solvent off and dry each one
Inspect each for bright scoring or a clipped edge — that is a strike, and it is a stop-work finding
Count all seven back in, rounded edge forward

cleaning.name: FRONT END CAP
tasks: Clean the residue build-up off the cap
Clean the threads specifically — that is where the seizing fouling sits
Check the end cap face for strike evidence
Dry and oil-free before it goes back on

cleaning.name: TUBE
tasks: Nylon brush the bore of the tube; the rear cap stays bonded in place
Never clamp the tube in a vise
Note any discolouration — it is the visible sign of excessive heat build-up
Dry and free of solvent before the baffles go back

reassembly: Confirm all seven baffles and the end cap are clean, dry and free of oil and solvent.
Install the seven baffles into the tube with the rounded edge facing forward.
Thread the front end cap into the tube and tighten it by hand using the suppressor wrench.
If your host is M9-.75 threaded, thread the adapter into the end cap and snug it with an adjustable wrench on the adapter flats.

Clear the host firearm, check the muzzle and suppressor threads are clean and that they match (1/2 x 28 TPI right hand unless the adapter is fitted), align them and screw the suppressor on as tight as you can by hand. Do not use the suppressor wrench to install it on the firearm.
fncheck: There is no dry-fire check for a suppressor — the check is a mounting and inspection check. With the host cleared, confirm the suppressor is fully threaded and hand-tight against the shoulder with no visible gap, that the baffle count was seven and each one showed no strike damage, and that nothing was added to the assembly that changes its overall length (that is unlawful under NFA rules). Once shooting, check frequently that the suppressor is still securely threaded to the firearm — SIG makes that a during-firing check, not an end-of-day one — and watch for tube discolouration as the sign it is being overheated.
